definitions.explanation: Describing someone who is intellectually sharp, quick-witted, or academically talented. The most common everyday way to say someone is smart in Japanese.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}は{頭|あたま}がいい。
{頭|あたま}がいい{人|ひと}は{説明|せつめい}が{上手|じょうず}だ。
examples.english: Smart people are good at explaining things.

examples.japanese: あの{子|こ}は{頭|あたま}がいいだけでなく、{運動|うんどう}もできる。
examples.english: That kid is not only smart but also good at sports.

notes:
Literally "head is good." The most natural and common way to express that someone is intelligent in casual Japanese. The opposite is {頭|あたま}が{悪|わる}い (not smart, slow-witted), which is quite blunt and can be offensive.

USAGE:
Used freely in conversation but avoided in formal writing, where {聡明|そうめい}な or {知的|ちてき}な is preferred. Can refer to academic intelligence, quick thinking, or practical cleverness depending on context. Sometimes used sarcastically: {頭|あたま}がいいね can mean "aren't you clever" in an ironic way.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {頭|あたま}がいい{人|ひと} — a smart person
- {頭|あたま}が{悪|わる}い — not smart, slow (opposite; blunt)
- {頭|あたま}の{良|よ}さ — smartness, intelligence
- {頭|あたま}の{良|い}い{子|こ} — a bright child

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {賢|かしこ}い — wise, clever (slightly more formal; includes practical wisdom)
- {聡明|そうめい}な — brilliant, sagacious (formal; literary)
- {利口|りこう}な — clever, shrewd (can imply street-smarts or being calculating)
